Chapter 3: Transforming Thought Patterns with Affirmations
Now that you’ve uncovered some of your emotional patterns, it’s time to talk about how you can actually shift them. This is where affirmations step in—they’re a powerful, hands-on way to change the thoughts you repeat to yourself, and, in turn, help your body heal.
So, what exactly are affirmations? Think of them as simple, positive statements you say with intention. They’re like tiny seeds you plant in your mind, slowly replacing old, limiting beliefs with ones that are supportive and empowering. Imagine a gardener pulling up weeds and planting new flowers—affirmations do just that for your self-doubt, fear, or resentment, and they make room for things like self-acceptance and hope.
Here’s why they work: affirmations help you change your inner dialogue. Most of us have a running background noise of self-criticism or worry—sometimes, we don’t even notice it. Over time, those thoughts become so familiar, it’s easy to mistake them for truth. Affirmations interrupt that pattern and offer you a new story to tell yourself.
Let’s say someone’s dealing with chronic fatigue. Maybe their mind keeps saying, “I’ll never have enough energy.” What if, instead, they gently introduced a new possibility by repeating, “I am filled with vitality and strength”? The more often they repeat it—especially during low-energy moments—the more their focus shifts from limitation to possibility.
Want to get the most out of affirmations? Here are a few tips to make them really work for you:
First, always state your affirmations in the present tense. Speak as though your change is happening right now. For example, swap out “I will be healthy” for “I am healthy and whole.”
Second, keep your affirmations positive and specific. Focus on what you want, not what you’re trying to avoid. Instead of “I’m not anxious,” try “I am calm and at peace.”
Third, repeat them regularly—and with feeling. The more consistent and emotionally engaged you are, the deeper these new thought patterns will take root.
And finally, pair your affirmations with real self-care. That might mean resting, eating nourishing food, or moving your body gently. These actions help reinforce the mental shift you’re creating.
Now, affirmations aren’t about ignoring reality or pretending challenges don’t exist. Instead, they’re about choosing to focus on your strengths and what’s possible, even when things feel tough. Over time, this practice can help you build a kinder, more supportive space inside yourself—one that makes healing a little bit easier.
It’s totally normal if you notice some resistance popping up. If an affirmation feels untrue or makes you uncomfortable, see if you can get curious about what beliefs it’s bumping up against. This process isn’t about forcing positivity—it’s about gently expanding what you believe could be true for you.
In this way, affirmations become a bridge between awareness and action. They take what you’ve learned about your emotional patterns and turn it into a daily practice—one that supports your well-being, both mentally and physically.
